judged_text: deleteEvent has the same self-contradictory fallback — find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) inside the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy — so calendarId is always undefined when the reference carries no external calendar id. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId calls calendar.events.delete with calendarId undefined, the API call throws, and the calendar event survives cancellation, leaving ghost events on hosts' calendars.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` compute the calendar id with an else-branch that cannot work: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else-branch), the predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined/null`, so it will almost always return `undefined` even when `event.destinationCalendar` contains valid calendars. That means the code fails to select the intended destination calendar when the reference lacks `externalCalendarId` (it will pass an undefined calendarId or fall back to something else depending on code not shown). The self-contradictory fallback described in the finding is directly present in the diff.
